1.1: This right here the word from the Lord that came to Joel, son of Pethuel.
1.2: Listen up, elders. And everybody else in the land—y'all need to hear this. Ain't nothin' like this ever happened in your lifetime? Or even your daddy's lifetime?
1.3: You better tell your kids about this, and make sure they tell their kids, and they pass it down again. This ain't somethin' to forget.
1.4: Whatever the chew-up locust ain't eat, the swarmin' ones did. Whatever the swarmin' ones missed, the crawlin' ones came for. And whatever they didn't get, the destroyin' ones cleaned up. Whole thing got wiped out, wave after wave.
1.5: Wake up, all y'all who stay drunk. Cry, all you wine sippers. That new wine y'all love? Gone. Ain't touchin' your lips no more.
1.6: A whole nation rolled up on My land—deep and ruthless. They got teeth like lions and jaws like beasts. They came to devour.
1.7: They done tore up My vineyard, crushed My fig trees. Stripped 'em bare, snapped off the branches, left nothin' but pale stubs.
1.8: Mourn like a young woman cryin' in her wedding dress 'cause her man gone too soon.
1.9: Ain't no grain offerings, no wine offerings at the temple no more. The priests, the ones who serve the Lord? Mournin'.
1.10: The fields? Ruined. The land itself mournin'. Grain? Wrecked. Wine? Dried up. Oil? Gone.
1.11: Y'all farmers better hang your heads. You vine workers? Wail. Ain't no wheat, ain't no barley. The harvest? Dead.
1.12: Vines shriveled. Fig trees dried up. Pomegranates, palms, apples—everything withered. Even joy done dried up from folks' hearts.
1.13: Priests, y'all better put on sackcloth and cry out. Stay up all night in mourning clothes, y'all who serve at God's altar. Ain't no offerings comin'. God's house sittin' empty.
1.14: Call a fast. Call a holy meeting. Get the elders, get everybody in the land. Bring 'em to the house of the Lord your God and cry out to Him.
1.15: Man, it's about to go down. The day of the Lord is right at the doorstep. And when it hits? It's gon' feel like the Almighty Himself came to tear it up.
1.16: Ain't food already cut off right in front of us? Ain't joy and celebration gone from God's house?
1.17: Seeds dried up under dirt clumps. Grain storage? Wrecked. Barns? Broken. Crops? Withered and gone.
1.18: The animals moanin' too. Cows wanderin' with no grass to eat. Even the sheep strugglin'. Starvin'.
1.19: Lord, I'm cryin' out to You. Fire burned the open land. Flames tore through every tree.
1.20: Even the wild animals lookin' to You, Lord. The rivers dried up, and flames swallowed the fields. Ain't nothin' left but ash and silence.

2.1: Blow that trumpet in Zion, y'all. Sound the alarm on God's holy hill. Everybody in the land—tremble. The Lord's day is comin'… and it's right around the corner.
2.2: It's gon' be a day full of darkness and thick clouds, like when the morning fog covers the mountains. A crew is comin'—big and strong—ain't never been none like it before, and there won't be nothin' like it again, not for generations.
2.3: In front of 'em, it's fire—burnin' everything. Behind 'em, flames—ain't nothin' left untouched. What used to look like Eden? Gon' be a wasteland by the time they done. Ain't nothin' escapin' this wave.
2.4: They look like horses. Run like warhorses too.
2.5: The sound they make? Like chariots crashin' across mountaintops. Like a wildfire tearin' through dry grass. Like a battle line movin' with purpose.
2.6: When folks see 'em, they panic. Faces go pale. Hearts drop.
2.7: They move like elite soldiers—climb walls like trained fighters. Each one stay in formation, no one outta line.
2.8: They don't bump into each other. They stay locked in their lane. Even when weapons fly, they still keep movin'. Ain't nothin' stoppin' 'em.
2.9: They run through the city, scale the walls, bust up in houses, crawl in through windows like thieves in the night.
2.10: The earth shakes underneath them. The skies start trembling. The sun and moon go dark, and the stars lose they shine.
2.11: The Lord's voice go before His army. His squad? Massive. The One carryin' out His Word? Unstoppable. The day of the Lord is huge… and terrifying. Who can handle it?
2.12: But even now, God sayin': "Turn to Me with your whole heart—fastin', cryin', mournin'."
2.13: Don't just rip your clothes—tear your heart open. Come back to the Lord your God. He's gracious. He's full of mercy. Slow to pop off, full of love. He might change His mind and hold back the judgment.
2.14: Who knows? He might leave behind a blessing— enough to give a grain offering and a drink offering to the Lord again.
2.15: Blow that trumpet in Zion again! Call a fast. Bring the whole squad together.
2.16: Get everybody—old folks, babies, toddlers. Tell the bride and groom to pause the honeymoon—this urgent.
2.17: Let the priests weep right between the porch and the altar. Let 'em beg: "Spare Your people, Lord! Don't let the world clown us. Don't let other nations say, 'Where yo God at now?'"
2.18: Then the Lord gon' get fired up for His land. He gon' feel that deep compassion for His people.
2.19: He gon' respond: "Look—I'm sendin' y'all grain, new wine, and oil again. Y'all gon' eat good, and I ain't lettin' nobody mock you no more."
2.20: That northern army? God gon' push 'em way out—into the desert. Their front gon' hit the eastern sea, their back fall in the western sea. And the stank from their bodies? It's gon' be strong 'cause they did some grimy things.
2.21: Don't be scared, land. Be glad and shout for joy— God done did somethin' amazing!
2.22: Don't trip, animals. The grass comin' back. The trees droppin' fruit again. The fig and vine got power again.
2.23: Y'all kids of Zion, start smilin' again. Rejoice in the Lord your God! He's sendin' that early rain again, just like He promised. And He got that later rain on the way too—all in the same season.
2.24: The threshin' floor? Gon' be packed with wheat. The wine vats? Overflowin' with wine and oil.
2.25: God said: "I'mma give back what the locusts stole from you— every wave: chewin', crawlin', swarmin', destroyin'. All that mess I let roll through? I'm restorin' it."
2.26: Y'all gon' eat good again. Full and satisfied. And y'all gon' praise the name of the Lord who did all this. And My people? They will never be ashamed again.
2.27: Then y'all gon' know—for real—that I'm right here in the middle of y'all. I'm the Lord your God, ain't no other. And again… My people will never be put to shame.
2.28: And after all that, God said: "I'ma pour out My Spirit on everybody. Sons and daughters gon' prophesy. Old men gon' dream dreams. Young men gon' see visions.
2.29: Even My servants—men and women both— gon' get that same Spirit."
2.30: "I'ma show wonders in the sky and on the earth— blood, fire, pillars of smoke.
2.31: The sun gon' turn dark, the moon gon' look like blood, right before the great and powerful day of the Lord shows up.
2.32: But listen—anybody who calls on the name of the Lord? They gon' be saved. Up on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, there's still gon' be deliverance— just like God said. Among the leftovers, the ones He called out by name… they gon' make it."

3.1: Look, when that time comes— when I bring My people back home, the ones from Judah and Jerusalem,
3.2: I'ma call all the nations together and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. That's where I'm settin' the record straight— judging them for what they did to My people, My inheritance, Israel. They scattered 'em all over and tried to split up My land like it was theirs.
3.3: They was gamblin' with My people— trade a boy for a prostitute, sell a girl just to get some wine to sip. Cold-hearted.
3.4: Yo, Tyre and Sidon, and all y'all from the Philistine coast— what y'all think y'all doin' messin' with Me? You think you gon' clap back at Me for something? If that's your plan, just know—I'ma hit back quick, and it's gon' fall hard on your own heads.
3.5: You stole My silver, My gold, took what was sacred and tossed it in your fake temples.
3.6: And you sold off My people—Judah and Jerusalem folk— shipped 'em off to Greece, just to wipe 'em off the map.
3.7: But check this: I'ma bring them back from where y'all sold 'em to. And I'ma bring that payback right back on you.
3.8: Your sons and daughters? I'ma hand 'em over to the people of Judah, and they gon' sell 'em off to the Sabeans, far away. The Lord done spoke on it.
3.9: Go ahead and announce this to the whole world: "Gear up! It's war time!" Wake up your soldiers. Get everybody who can fight—pull up.
3.10: Turn your farm tools into weapons. Grab them plowshares and turn 'em into swords. Take them pruning hooks and turn 'em into spears. Even the weak ones gotta say, "I'm strong now!"
3.11: Gather up, all you nations. Come stand in this place. Lord, send down Your mighty ones!
3.12: Let the nations rise up and meet Me in the Valley of Jehoshaphat. That's where I'ma judge all them enemies surrounding My people.
3.13: Swing the sickle—the harvest is ready. Step on down into the winepress. It's overflowin' with wickedness. It's time.
3.14: Crowds on top of crowds in the valley of decision. The day of the Lord is close—real close—in that place of reckoning.
3.15: The sun and moon gon' go dark. The stars gon' fade out too.
3.16: But the Lord? He gon' roar loud from Zion. His voice from Jerusalem gon' shake the skies and the ground. But His people? He gon' be their shelter. He gon' be the strength for all His children.
3.17: You gon' know I'm the Lord your God, livin' right in Zion, My holy mountain. Jerusalem gon' be holy again. Ain't no foreigners messin' it up no more.
3.18: When that day hits, the mountains gon' drip with wine, the hills gon' flow with milk, and streams gon' overflow through Judah. A fresh fountain gon' spring up from the Lord's house and bless the whole Valley of Acacias.
3.19: Egypt gon' be nothin' but ruins. Edom gon' be a dry, dead place. Why? 'Cause they brought violence to Judah, sheddin' innocent blood in God's land.
3.20: But Judah? Judah gon' last forever. Jerusalem gon' stand strong for every generation.
3.21: And I'ma clear My people of all the bloodshed. I held it for a time, but now? I'm cleanin' it up. I'm livin' in Zion.
